title: Linear classifiers, discriminants, and logistic models

items.title: Finite linear-score classifiers with a deterministic tie rule
items.statement: Let $d\ge1$ and $K\ge2$ be finite integers, with ordered labels $1<2<\cdots<K$. A finite linear-score classifier on $\mathbb R^d$ is specified by vectors $a_k\in\mathbb R^d$ and constants $b_k\in\mathbb R$, one pair for each label, and assigns score $s_k(x)=a_k^Tx+b_k$ to $x\in\mathbb R^d$. Its predicted label is the smallest index attaining $\max_{1\le j\le K}s_j(x)$. This rule is single-valued, including when two or more scores tie.
items.strategy: Define affine scores on an ordered finite class set and the smallest-index argmax tie rule.

references.title: Hastie, Tibshirani, and Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed., corrected 12th printing

items.title: Indicator-response least-squares classification
items.statement: Let $n,q\ge1$ and $K\ge2$ be finite integers. For a fixed design matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}$ and labels $y_i\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$, form the indicator response matrix $Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times K}$ by $Y_{ik}=1$ when $y_i=k$ and $Y_{ik}=0$ otherwise. For a coefficient matrix $B\in\mathbb R^{q\times K}$, set $L(B)=(2n)^{-1}\|Y-XB\|_F^2$, where $\|A\|_F^2$ is the sum of squares of all entries of $A$. Let $B_*$ be the least-squares minimizer with smallest Frobenius norm. For a new row vector $x^T\in\mathbb R^{1\times q}$, the indicator-response classifier assigns scores $(x^TB_*)_k$ and predicts the smallest class index attaining their maximum. An intercept, if used, is one of the columns of $X$; no rank assumption is imposed on $X$.
items.strategy: Define the one-hot response matrix, squared-error objective, and deterministic minimum-Frobenius-norm fit; its existence is discharged by the local lemma.

references.title: Hastie, Tibshirani, and Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed., corrected 12th printing
Stanford CS229 Spring 2022 lecture notes

items.title: The minimum-norm indicator-response least-squares fit exists uniquely
items.statement: Let $n,q\ge1$ and $K\ge2$ be finite, let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}$, and let $Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times K}$ be an indicator response matrix. Among all minimizers of $\|Y-XB\|_F^2$ over $B\in\mathbb R^{q\times K}$ there is a unique one of smallest Frobenius norm. If $X=U_rD_rV_r^T$ is a thin singular-value decomposition with rank $r>0$, orthonormal columns in $U_r,V_r$, and positive diagonal entries in $D_r$, then this minimizer is $B_*=V_rD_r^{-1}U_r^TY$. If $r=0$, then $X=0$ and $B_*=0$. In either case the full minimizer set is $\{B_*+N:XN=0\}$.
items.strategy: Use SVD to construct the projection fit, then the least-squares normal equation and row-space/kernel orthogonality to prove the unique minimum-norm property.

references.title: Hastie, Tibshirani, and Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed., corrected 12th printing

items.title: Gaussian LDA and QDA model contracts
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$ and $K\ge2$ be finite integers, let the class label be $Y\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$, and let $X\in\mathbb R^d$. Choose class priors $\pi_k>0$ with $\sum_{k=1}^K\pi_k=1$, means $\mu_k\in\mathbb R^d$, and real symmetric positive-definite covariance matrices $\Sigma_k\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$. The Gaussian generative model has $\Pr(Y=k)=\pi_k$ and conditional laws $X\mid Y=k\sim N_d(\mu_k,\Sigma_k)$. The LDA subfamily imposes one common covariance matrix, $\Sigma_k=\Sigma$ for every $k$; the QDA subfamily permits the covariance matrices to differ by class.
items.strategy: Specify finite Gaussian classes, positive priors, the shared versus class-specific positive-definite covariance conventions, and the AC premise.

references.title: Hastie, Tibshirani, and Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed., corrected 12th printing

items.title: Common-covariance LDA scores are affine and QDA scores are quadratic
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge1$ and $K\ge2$ be finite, let $\pi_k>0$ with $\sum_{k=1}^K\pi_k=1$, let $\mu_k\in\mathbb R^d$, and let each real symmetric matrix $\Sigma_k\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ be positive definite, meaning $v^T\Sigma_kv>0$ for every nonzero $v$. Define
$$
f_k(x)=(2\pi)^{-d/2}\det(\Sigma_k)^{-1/2}\exp\!\left(-\tfrac12(x-\mu_k)^T\Sigma_k^{-1}(x-\mu_k)\right),\qquad p_k(x)=\frac{\pi_k f_k(x)}{\sum_{j=1}^K\pi_jf_j(x)}.
$$
For LDA, assume $\Sigma_k=\Sigma$ for all $k$; then $\log p_k(x)$ differs by a term independent of $k$ from the affine score
$$
\delta_k^{\mathrm L}(x)=x^T\Sigma^{-1}\mu_k-\tfrac12\mu_k^T\Sigma^{-1}\mu_k+\log\pi_k.
$$
For QDA, allow the $\Sigma_k$ to vary with $k$; then $\log p_k(x)$ differs by a term independent of $k$ from the quadratic score
$$
\delta_k^{\mathrm Q}(x)=-\tfrac12\log\det(\Sigma_k)-\tfrac12(x-\mu_k)^T\Sigma_k^{-1}(x-\mu_k)+\log\pi_k.
$$
Thus maximizing the posterior probabilities uses affine scores in LDA and scores of degree at most two in QDA; ties are resolved by the smallest class index.
items.strategy: Apply the positive-definite Gaussian density theorem, form the density Bayes ratio, expand its quadratic, and cancel only class-independent terms.

items.title: Binary logistic and multiclass softmax conditional models
items.statement: For $d\ge1$, define the sigmoid $\sigma(t)=(1+e^{-t})^{-1}$. A binary logistic conditional model on $x\in\mathbb R^d$ has finite coefficients $\beta_0\in\mathbb R$, $\beta\in\mathbb R^d$ and specifies $\Pr(Y=1\mid x)=\sigma(\beta_0+x^T\beta)$ and $\Pr(Y=0\mid x)=1-\sigma(\beta_0+x^T\beta)$ for $Y\in\{0,1\}$. Its classifier predicts $1$ when $\beta_0+x^T\beta>0$ and predicts $0$ when $\beta_0+x^T\beta\le0$. A multiclass softmax conditional model has finite ordered labels $1,\ldots,K$ with $K\ge2$, affine logits $\eta_k(x)=a_k+x^Tw_k$ for $a_k\in\mathbb R$ and $w_k\in\mathbb R^d$, and probabilities $\Pr(Y=k\mid x)=e^{\eta_k(x)}/\sum_{j=1}^K e^{\eta_j(x)}$; its classifier chooses the smallest index attaining the largest logit. These models specify conditional label probabilities and impose no distributional assumption on the feature vector $X$, in particular no Gaussian feature law.
items.strategy: Define conditional Bernoulli logistic and multiclass softmax probabilities, tie rules, and the absence of a marginal feature-law assumption.

items.title: Binary logistic log-likelihood and L1-penalized objective
items.statement:
Fix a finite design with rows $x_i^T\in\mathbb R^q$, $1\le i\le n$, where $n\ge1$ and $q\ge1$. Use either an intercept design, in which the first coordinate of every row is $1$ and $\beta=(\beta_0,\theta)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^{q-1}$, or a no-intercept design, in which no coordinate is reserved as an intercept, the intercept coefficient is fixed at zero, and $\beta\in\mathbb R^q$. Let $y_i\in\{0,1\}$ and assume the responses are conditionally independent given the design, with binary logistic probabilities $p_i=\sigma(x_i^T\beta)$ for finite coefficients. In either design convention, the log-likelihood is
$$
\ell(\beta)=\sum_{i=1}^n\left[y_i x_i^T\beta-\log\!\left(1+e^{x_i^T\beta}\right)\right].
$$
For $\lambda>0$, the L1 objective to minimize in the intercept design is $-\ell(\beta)+\lambda\|\theta\|_1$, so the intercept is unpenalized; in the no-intercept design it is $-\ell(\beta)+\lambda\|\beta\|_1$, so every coefficient is penalized. Here $\|\theta\|_1=\sum_{j=1}^{q-1}|\theta_j|$ and $\|\beta\|_1=\sum_{j=1}^{q}|\beta_j|$, with an empty sum equal to zero. These are objective definitions and assert no optimizer existence.
items.strategy: Write the independent fixed-design Bernoulli log-likelihood and distinguish an unpenalized intercept from the all-coordinate L1 convention.

items.title: Binary logistic derivatives and the exact Newton/IRLS update
items.statement:
Let $n,q\ge1$ be finite, let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times q}$ be a fixed design matrix whose first column is the intercept column of ones, and let $y\in\{0,1\}^n$. For finite $\beta\in\mathbb R^q$, put $\eta=X\beta$, $p_i=\sigma(\eta_i)$, $W=\operatorname{diag}(p_i(1-p_i))$, and $\ell(\beta)=\sum_i[y_i\eta_i-\log(1+e^{\eta_i})]$. Then
$$
\nabla\ell(\beta)=X^T(y-p),\qquad \nabla^2\ell(\beta)=-X^TWX.
$$
The diagonal entries of $W$ are positive, so $-\ell$ is convex; if $X$ has full column rank, $X^TWX$ is positive definite. In that full-rank case, the exact Newton step for maximizing the unpenalized log-likelihood is
$$
\beta_{\mathrm{new}}=\beta+(X^TWX)^{-1}X^T(y-p)=(X^TWX)^{-1}X^TWz,\qquad z=X\beta+W^{-1}(y-p).
$$
This is the Bernoulli-logit IRLS step with the weighted least-squares convention using weights $p_i(1-p_i)$. The identities describe one update and do not assert convergence of repeated updates.
items.strategy: Differentiate the scalar likelihood, establish W positivity and rank conditions, verify the Bernoulli GLM hypotheses, and identify the weighted least-squares IRLS output with the Newton solve.

items.title: Complete separation gives an unattained logistic likelihood supremum
items.statement: Let $n,q\ge1$ be finite, let $x_i\in\mathbb R^q$ be a fixed design row with an intercept coordinate when one is used, and let $y_i\in\{0,1\}$. Suppose the unpenalized binary logistic log-likelihood is $\ell(\beta)=\sum_i[y_i x_i^T\beta-\log(1+e^{x_i^T\beta})]$. If there is a vector $v\in\mathbb R^q$ such that $(2y_i-1)x_i^Tv>0$ for every $i$, then $\sup_{\beta\in\mathbb R^q}\ell(\beta)=0$, and no finite coefficient vector attains this supremum.
items.strategy: Scale a strict separating vector to make each likelihood term approach zero, then show every finite coefficient has strictly negative likelihood.

items.title: The cyclic perceptron update procedure
items.statement: Input a finite ordered sample $((x_i,y_i))_{i=1}^n$ with $n\ge1$, $x_i\in\mathbb R^d$, and $y_i\in\{-1,+1\}$. Put $\widetilde x_i=(x_i,1)\in\mathbb R^{d+1}$ and initialize $w=0$. In each pass, visit $i=1,\ldots,n$ in the fixed order. Whenever $y_iw^T\widetilde x_i\le0$, replace $w$ by $w+y_i\widetilde x_i$ and count one update. After a full pass with no updates, stop and return $w$. The associated classifier returns $+1$ when $w^T(x,1)>0$ and $-1$ when $w^T(x,1)\le0$, so a score tie is assigned to $-1$. The procedure has no iteration limit; if its stop condition never holds, it continues with further passes.
items.strategy: Specify the finite ordered sample, augmented bias coordinate, zero initialization, exact non-strict update and full-pass stop rule without a convergence claim.

items.title: The perceptron makes at most R squared over gamma squared mistakes
items.statement: Let $((x_i,y_i))_{i=1}^n$ be a finite ordered sample with $n\ge1$, $x_i\in\mathbb R^d$, and $y_i\in\{-1,+1\}$. Put $\widetilde x_i=(x_i,1)\in\mathbb R^{d+1}$, with Euclidean inner product $\langle u,v\rangle=u^Tv$ and norm $\|u\|_2=(u^Tu)^{1/2}$. Suppose $\|\widetilde x_i\|_2\le R$ for every $i$ and there is a unit vector $u\in\mathbb R^{d+1}$ and $\gamma>0$ such that $y_i\langle u,\widetilde x_i\rangle\ge\gamma$ for every $i$. The zero-initialized cyclic procedure that visits the sample in the stated order and updates $w\leftarrow w+y_i\widetilde x_i$ whenever $y_i\langle w,\widetilde x_i\rangle\le0$ makes at most $R^2/\gamma^2$ updates and stops after a finite pass with no updates. At each visit, before its update, the procedure predicts $+1$ if $\langle w,\widetilde x_i\rangle>0$ and $-1$ otherwise; a prediction mistake is a visit on which this prediction differs from $y_i$. The total number of such mistakes before termination is at most $R^2/\gamma^2$. The returned weight vector has strictly positive signed margin on every sample point.
items.strategy: Accumulate separator progress and bound squared norm at each update, combine the inequalities by Cauchy–Schwarz, and deduce finite termination.

items.title: A strictly separated two-point sample has an unattained logistic likelihood supremum
items.statement: Take two one-dimensional observations $(x_1,y_1)=(-1,0)$ and $(x_2,y_2)=(1,1)$ with an intercept in the design. The augmented rows are $(1,-1)$ and $(1,1)$, and the vector $(0,1)$ strictly separates them. Along coefficients $\beta(t)=(0,t)$ with $t>0$, the log-likelihood is $-2\log(1+e^{-t})$, which tends to zero while remaining negative for every finite $t$. The sample therefore has an unattained supremum at zero.
items.strategy: Verify a strict separator and compute the diverging-slope log-likelihood explicitly.

items.title: Two contradictory labels make the cyclic perceptron repeat a two-pass cycle
items.statement: Use the ordered one-dimensional sample $(x_1,y_1)=(0,+1)$, $(x_2,y_2)=(0,-1)$. It is not separable by an affine score because both observations have the same augmented input $(0,1)$ and require opposite strict signs. For the zero-initialized cyclic perceptron, every pass updates on both observations and returns the weight vector to zero, so no no-update pass occurs.
items.strategy: Apply both updates in order and show that every pass returns to the zero weight vector.
